simple.meaning: עֲרוּגָה (ʻărûwgâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “something piled up (as if (figuratively) raised by mental aspiration) , i.e. a paterre.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עֲרוּגָה (H6170) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Song of Songs 5:13, with occurrences in Song of Solomon, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲרוּגָה (H6170) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עֲרוּגָה (H6170) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עֲרוּגָה (ʻărûwgâh) / H6170 is traced through Song of Songs 5:13, Song of Songs 6:2, Ezekiel 17:7, Ezekiel 17:10 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

timeline.evidenceText: “ ‘ “There was also another great eagle with great wings and many feathers. Behold, this vine bent its roots toward him, and shot out its branches toward him, from the beds of its plantation, that he might water it.
Yes, behold, being planted, will it prosper? Won’t it utterly wither when the east wind touches it? It will wither in the beds where it grew.” ’ ”
